name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Courtney holds a large fundraising edge ($760K raised, $603K on hand vs. $284K for Austin)
District leans Democratic (D+4) with a favorable national environment for Democrats
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
No public polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Courtney combines incumbency, a three-to-one money advantage, and a D+4 district in a favorable environment, and prediction markets price his win chances near 97%. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race, or significant outside spending against Courtney, would warrant revisiting the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Connecticut's 2nd District pairs a Democratic-leaning electorate with a well-established incumbent. Joe Courtney has represented the seat since 2007 and enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $760,000 to George Austin's $284,000 and holding more than three times the cash on hand. Outside spending has been minimal, with only a small amount supporting Courtney.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Courtney's chances near 97%, and the district's four-point Democratic lean combined with a favorable national environment points to a comfortable margin. Austin would need a substantial shift in the race's dynamics to close the gap; as things stand, the seat is on track to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin.
